topics.summary: On November 20, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann hypothesis as a 17-million-line Lean library, made working with Claude, and the Lean and Mathlib communities certified it as correct the next day.
topics.why_now: Two attempts landed the same day: Alpöge's machine-checked proof, and a 940-page human-written manuscript by Alessandro Masullo aimed at the generalized hypothesis, which readers have since found gaps in. The Hacker News thread on Masullo's announcement drew 2,447 points.

topics.name: full moon beaver moon
topics.summary: The Beaver Moon is the traditional name for November's full moon. In 2026 it reached peak fullness at 14:53 UTC on November 24 and counts as a supermoon.
topics.why_now: The full moon peaked today, November 24, and Space.com describes it as a supermoon.

aliases: Stalwart is now a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange
topics.summary: Stalwart, an open source mail server, says version 1.2.0 released November 23, 2026 can stand in for Microsoft Exchange by speaking Exchange's client protocols. Commenters dispute the phrase drop-in.
topics.why_now: The project's announcement post, titled with the drop-in claim, reached the top of Hacker News on release day.

topics.name: thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini
topics.summary: Inkling 2 Mini is an open-weights model Thinking Machines Lab released on November 20 under the Apache 2.0 license: a 26.4B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 3.4B active, built to run on local hardware such as Macs with 32 GB or more.
topics.why_now: A Hacker News post titled "Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory" drew 582 points. That 5.4 GB figure belongs to an independent compressed build, not the official release, whose checkpoint is about 20 GB.

editorial.brief: Grand Theft Auto VI was the most travelled subject of the day, turning up on Wikipedia, YouTube, Google Trends and Lemmy, where a headline had reverse engineers running it on PC against its publisher's wishes. Two Avengers: Doomsday spots built on Magneto and Doctor Doom drew 3.8 million YouTube views between them. Wikipedia's top read, meanwhile, was a guitarist.
editorial.cover_sub: Andy Taylor, guitarist, was read 318,400 times, with Duran Duran fifth on the same list, while the rest of the web busied itself with Grand Theft Auto VI and a Doomsday trailer.
editorial.wiki_deck: A guitarist outread a Hindu epic and two men from American football. The margin was modest, the reason unstated, and the band he played in sat fifth.
editorial.letter_headline: Grand Theft Auto everywhere, a guitarist on top
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is warming to self-hosting and grumbling about hard drive prices. Lemmy cheers a Ukrainian student's GPS-free drone autopilot. Bluesky shares printmakers and a free Thanksgiving meal. Mastodon is urgent about strokes, cross about IBM.
editorial.foreign_deck: Asian stocks fell on a stalled AI rebound and the UN chief sought AI talks, while America searched Kuwait, Britain Martin Lewis and India SAP layoffs.
editorial.markets_deck: A coin toss on Bitcoin ending between $60,000 and $62,000 led with $2M traded. Behind it: Counter-Strike, a Fed hold priced at 4 per cent, and Taipei's mayoralty.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,140,407 players, with Dota 2 and PUBG behind and ROB RUN at 388,351. On Twitch, TheBurntPeanut held 41,534 viewers, more than triple the PGL broadcast.
editorial.yt_headline: A Doomsday trailer selling cinema tickets
editorial.yt_note: Avengers: Doomsday holds two of five places, both built on Magneto and Doctor Doom. Alongside sit an Anuel AA visualiser at 1.57 million views and a duck hunt at 983,488.
editorial.closing_note: By tomorrow the salad question will have been answered, the Bitcoin market settled, and Andy Taylor will have returned to the ordinary traffic of Wikipedia. Grand Theft Auto VI, seen on four feeds at once, will probably not have the decency to leave.
wiki_paras: Andy Taylor, guitarist, was Wikipedia's most read article, at 318,400 views. Second was Ramayana: Part 1 with 256,714, which leaves a lead of 1.2 times. That is a win on points rather than a knockout. Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy filled the next two places, a pair of football names some 4,000 views apart.

The list supplies its own footnote. Duran Duran, the band Taylor played guitar for, sits fifth with 164,045 views, so a good many readers appear to have followed one thread from the man to the group. What started them down it is not recorded here. No news wire, trend or trending video in the snapshot mentions him.

What it says about the day is that attention was split. The cross-feed noise belonged to a video game and a superhero trailer, neither of which reached Wikipedia's top five. Encyclopaedia readers went their own way, towards a guitarist, an Indian epic on film and the NFL. Nobody asked them to agree.
letter_paras: This was a scattered day with one recurring guest. Grand Theft Auto VI turned up on Wikipedia, YouTube, Google Trends and Lemmy, the last with a headline about reverse engineers running it on PC. The Avengers: Doomsday trailers did the same double act across Wikipedia and YouTube. Everything else kept to its own feed and minded its own business.

In the unglamorous corners, Polymarket listed a market on Shakhtar Donetsk winning the Champions League, priced at 0 per cent with too little money behind it to register. The largest of 25 earthquakes struck near the Revilla Gigedo Islands at magnitude 5.7. On Lemmy, a question about the most unusual salad anyone had seen scored 649.

Taking every feed in the same minute is the only fair way to compare them. A trailer, a guitarist and a salad have nothing in common except the minute they were noticed, and that is enough to make them comparable. Tomorrow the same clock will run again, and the differences will be the news.
